items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the autobiographical extract 'Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom', and answer.

"A young lawyer once believed that freedom meant being able to stay out late, to read what he liked and to travel where he wished. Then he saw that his neighbours could not walk on certain streets, could not sit on certain benches, could not dream certain dreams. From that day his small, private freedom no longer satisfied him. He wanted it for everyone, or he did not want it at all."

Which of Mandela's ideas does this passage echo?

items.markingKey: His hunger for his own freedom became a hunger for the freedom of his people. (1–2 marks for a complete answer.)

items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the autobiographical extract 'Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom', and answer.

"A young lawyer once believed that freedom meant being able to stay out late, to read what he liked and to travel where he wished. Then he saw that his neighbours could not walk on certain streets, could not sit on certain benches, could not dream certain dreams. From that day his small, private freedom no longer satisfied him. He wanted it for everyone, or he did not want it at all."

Answer the following:
(i) What did freedom mean to the young lawyer at first?
(ii) What made him change his idea of freedom?  (a) A holiday abroad  (b) A new job  (c) Seeing that his neighbours were denied basic rights  (d) A long illness
(iii) What does "he wanted it for everyone, or he did not want it at all" show?
(iv) The word "private" here is the opposite of …  (a) shared  (b) secret  (c) personal  (d) quiet
items.answer: (i) Personal liberties – staying out late, reading what he liked, travelling freely. (ii) (c) Seeing that his neighbours were denied basic rights (iii) His personal freedom became meaningless unless all his people were free. (iv) (a) shared
items.markingKey: (i) Personal liberties – staying out late, reading what he liked, travelling freely. (ii) (c) Seeing that his neighbours were denied basic rights (iii) His personal freedom became meaningless unless all his people were free. (iv) (a) shared (1 mark each, 4 marks.)
